newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds slide with international markets.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds slide with international markets.

text.p: 1515 GMT - Austrian bonds ended weaker amid meagre volumes on Thursday, and traders said higher U.S. jobless figures had negligible impact, coming in line with expectations.
"There was nothing going on in the morning and then in the afternoon it was even quieter," one trader said.
The German Bund future tested support at 100 points.
"If we fall below that level, I reckon the next support will be at 99.60 points," another said, noting that as long as the Bund future stayed above 100 all looked rosy.
* 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 down 10 bps at 98.10 to yield 5.88 pct (5.87) in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 98.15/25 to yield 5.88/86.
* Latest five-year 4.375 bond maturing February 2002 closed down five bps at 98.30 in bourse trade to yield 4.71 pct (4.70), quoted post-market at 98.26/36 to yield 4.72/70 percent.
* Austrian bond futures down 24 bps at 107.20 on turnover of 693 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany one bp lower at minus three bps, five-year spread down three at five bps.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.400 and overnight money at 3.15/3.40. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
